subject: Monarch Butterfly
fact: Monarch butterflies migrate long distances between seasonal habitats.

subject: Swallowtail Butterfly
fact: Many swallowtail butterflies have tail-like extensions on their hind wings.

subject: Painted Lady Butterfly
fact: Painted lady butterflies live on every continent except Antarctica.

subject: Blue Morpho Butterfly
fact: Blue morpho wings look brilliant blue because of tiny structures that reflect light.

subject: Luna Moth
fact: Luna moths have pale green wings and long tails on their hind wings.

subject: Atlas Moth
fact: Atlas moths are among the largest moths in the world.

subject: Cecropia Moth
fact: Cecropia moths are the largest native moths in North America.

subject: Honey Bee
fact: Honey bees communicate the location of food with a movement called a waggle dance.

subject: Bumblebee
fact: Bumblebees can vibrate flowers to shake loose pollen.

subject: Carpenter Bee
fact: Carpenter bees make nesting tunnels in wood.

subject: Paper Wasp
fact: Paper wasps build open nests from chewed wood fibers mixed with saliva.

subject: Bald-Faced Hornet
fact: Bald-faced hornets build large gray paper nests above the ground.

subject: Ladybug
fact: Ladybugs are beetles that often eat plant pests such as aphids.

subject: Firefly
fact: Fireflies make light inside their bodies through a chemical reaction.

subject: Stag Beetle
fact: Male stag beetles have large jaws that can look like deer antlers.

subject: Rhinoceros Beetle
fact: Rhinoceros beetles are named for the horn-like structures on their heads.

subject: Dung Beetle
fact: Some dung beetles roll balls of animal dung to use as food or nesting material.

subject: Click Beetle
fact: Click beetles can snap their bodies and spring into the air when lying on their backs.

subject: Weevil
fact: Weevils are beetles with long snout-like mouths.

subject: Dragonfly
fact: Dragonflies can fly forward, backward, and hover in place.

subject: Damselfly
fact: Damselflies usually fold their wings together above their bodies when resting.

subject: Grasshopper
fact: Grasshoppers have powerful back legs for jumping.

subject: Field Cricket
fact: Male crickets chirp by rubbing parts of their wings together.

subject: Katydid
fact: Many katydids look like leaves, which helps them hide among plants.

subject: Praying Mantis
fact: Praying mantises hold their front legs folded and use them to grab prey.

subject: Walking Stick
fact: Walking sticks use twig-like bodies as camouflage.

subject: Leaf Insect
fact: Leaf insects have flat green bodies that resemble leaves.

subject: Cicada
fact: Male cicadas make loud buzzing songs using special organs on their bodies.

subject: Aphid
fact: Aphids use needle-like mouthparts to drink sap from plants.

subject: Black Garden Ant
fact: Ant colonies can include workers, queens, and developing young.

subject: Leafcutter Ant
fact: Leafcutter ants carry pieces of leaves underground to grow fungus for food.

subject: Termite
fact: Termites live in colonies and are important recyclers of dead plant material.

subject: Mosquito
fact: Only female mosquitoes of many species drink blood; both sexes also feed on plant sugars.

subject: Housefly
fact: Houseflies can taste food with sensors on their feet.

subject: Fruit Fly
fact: Fruit flies are attracted to ripe or fermenting fruit.

subject: Horsefly
fact: Horseflies have very large compound eyes.

subject: Green Lacewing
fact: Lacewing larvae eat many small plant pests such as aphids.

subject: Mayfly
fact: Adult mayflies live briefly, while their young can spend much longer living in water.

subject: Caddisfly
fact: Many caddisfly larvae build protective cases from sand, twigs, or other tiny materials.

subject: Earwig
fact: Earwigs have pincer-like structures at the ends of their abdomens.

subject: Silverfish
fact: Silverfish are wingless insects with shiny scales and three tail-like bristles.

subject: Flea
fact: Fleas can jump many times their own body length.

subject: Water Strider
fact: Water striders can skate across the surface of ponds without sinking.

subject: Water Boatman
fact: Water boatmen are aquatic insects that swim using oar-like hind legs.

subject: Diving Beetle
fact: Predaceous diving beetles are strong swimmers and carry air underwater.

subject: Whirligig Beetle
fact: Whirligig beetles spin quickly across the surface of ponds in groups.

subject: Spittlebug
fact: Spittlebug young hide inside bubbly foam on plant stems.

subject: Shield Bug
fact: Shield bugs have broad bodies shaped a little like shields.

subject: Assassin Bug
fact: Assassin bugs use a pointed beak to capture and feed on other small animals.

subject: Stink Bug
fact: Many stink bugs release a strong-smelling chemical when disturbed.

subject: Lanternfly
fact: Lanternflies are plant-feeding insects with striking wings and colors.

subject: Dobsonfly
fact: Adult dobsonflies have large wings, and males of some species have very long jaws.

subject: Mole Cricket
fact: Mole crickets have shovel-like front legs made for digging.

subject: Jerusalem Cricket
fact: Jerusalem crickets are large wingless insects that spend much of their time underground.

subject: Jumping Spider
fact: Jumping spiders have excellent eyesight and leap onto prey.

subject: Orb-Weaver Spider
fact: Orb-weaver spiders build round wheel-shaped webs.

subject: Tarantula
fact: Tarantulas are large hairy spiders that usually hunt from the ground.

subject: Scorpion
fact: Scorpions have pincers and a curved tail tipped with a stinger.

subject: Centipede
fact: Centipedes have one pair of legs on each body segment.

subject: Millipede
fact: Millipedes have two pairs of legs on most body segments and often curl up for protection.
